CA States NARP Report

  • Quote

    Post by rsersen » July 31st, 2017, 3:41 am

    Just got home from a pretty awesome time at CA States, and want to get this all down before I forget the details.

    I'll keep my backstory brief. I returned to SWCCG at the beginning of this year, for the same reasons as many others - new movies, nostalgia, etc. Only intended to be a collector, but as I started accumulating cards and lurking around the forums, I got the itch to build decks and play again. This was about the same time that GEMP started getting caught up to the current card pool, and that played a huge role in getting me back up to speed. I can't say enough good things about that platform, and it was great to meet batmouse and thank him in person. Without it, I'd almost certainly still be focused on collecting, and I wouldn't even be writing this.

    So after a few months and a couple hundred GEMP games, I decide it's time to start playing with real cards. This is a big step for me, because aside from solo play, I legitimately haven't played an game in-person since middle school. Much less an actual event. When the SoCal Super Weekend was announced, it seemed like a pretty good opportunity to get over that hump. It's only an hour flight from Oakland, I had Southwest points to burn, and the shop is only a couple miles from the airport. I figure what the hell, no time like the present, and I sign up for CA States on Sunday.

    I decide right away that I'm only going to play with decks I can build myself. I know the community is great about lending to people. But without knowing how much time I'd have between landing and the first game, I wanted to spend that time meeting people and settling in. Not rushing around to find cards, sleeving them, and trying to throw together a deck at the last second.

    For light side, I settle on Diplo pretty quickly. I've been playing a version that includes Lando+Falcon for a turn 1 delivery, and speeders on the ground. It fares pretty well on GEMP, with no terribly bad matchups. I just hope not to see a lot of IE at the event.

    Dark side is a little tougher. I debate between CCT Scum (using Boba-v to flip) or Jonny Chu's First Order Dark Deal. Initially I pick CCT, but after some playtesting, it just feels really fragile. And it has some downright awful matchups against TRM and Jakku CPv, both of which I'm expecting to see. Plus, I just really don't have that much fun playing it.

    So I turn to Dark Deal. This deck doesn't have the element of surprise that it used to. But I have a hell of a lot of fun playing it. I have zero expectations of winning this event, so I may as well go with a deck I enjoy. I make a few tech tweaks - Ysanne for Jyn, EPP Vader for TIGIH, and since I'm adding more leaders, might as well throw in GMT(v). It goes 8-4 in playtesting on GEMP, and now I'm feeling decent about both of my choices.

    Sunday morning I'm off to the airport. After a quick 50 minute flight, I land at Burbank and grab an Uber to the shop. There's about 30 minutes until the first game, which works out perfectly for me to meet the crew and get settled in. That's enough rambling, on to the cards.

    Game 1 - Diplo Speeders vs Adam's IE Walkers

    I was hoping not to see IE today, so of course it's the first matchup. I'm pretty nervous as I sit down and get ready to put real cards on a table for the first time in forever. But Adam's a super chill guy to play against, and that quickly dissipates.

    Surprisingly, he doesn't battle Tantive on turn 1, choosing to put Ozzel at the Executor DB, and shuttling Tarkin up from Tatooine to play Alert My Star Destroyer. I use Lando+Falcon to deliver the Plans on turn 1, grab Artoo I Have A Bad Feeling About This from Reserve, and move back to Tatooine ready for a fight. Next turn he gets guys/vehicles on the ground to flip, battles in space. He draws none, I draw a 1, it's a tie. On my turn 2 I flip myself, and spread out to flip him back 0. For the rest of the game I stay spread out, keep him on the 0 side, and take advantage of high attrition to clear him off sites. Devastator abandons Tatooine and Occupation never hits the table. Eventually he does get Flagship Executor and Devastator back to Tatooine (I had Punch It! and AIHABFAT in hand if he had battled), but at that point it's too late to make a difference.

    Win (1-0)

    Game 2 - First Order Deal vs Adam's HB

    I've played a lot of games with Deal, but this is one matchup I'm not familiar with. All I know is that I only have three starfighters in the deck, and I have no intention of sacrificing those to battles/probing. So I know upfront it'll be a drain race and I just try to get Deal set up as quick as I can.

    This game is a great example of how online and real play are totally different beasts. As often as I've done this on GEMP, keeping track of all the various puzzle pieces I need is a bit overwhelming in person, and I totally screw up the third turn. I think I can pull this off with just Phasma and Kylo, counting on two Used pulls....and then realize that one of them would need to go to the Tower where they won't get the pull. Dammit. Now I'm flustered and trying to figure out a backup plan. So I put both at the docking bay and for reasons I still can't explain, use the second pull on a trooper (for Strategic Reserves) instead of a TIE. That ends up being the difference maker, as it takes me another 2-3 turns to draw up a TIE. It also takes Adam a little longer than usual to flip, since he activates two systems and has to dig them out of the bottom of his Force pile. But by the time I finally get Deal out, he's flipped, cancelling drains, and I've run out of troopers to block his. This still ends up being a really close game, and without that early screw-up I might have pulled it out. Lesson learned.

    Loss (1-1)

    Game 3 - Diplo Speeders vs Batmouse's Court

    I don't remember much from this game because it was such a total ass-kicking, and was over almost as soon as it started. I would say I just crapped the bed, but I don't want to take any credit away from Batmouse - he's the regional champ for a reason.

    Game starts out routinely enough, but then I go on the offensive way too early, and battle Rogue 1 with Commie Luke against Jodo (who I forget can cancel a destiny) and BFBH. I limit him to one draw with Combined Fleet Action, but he reacts Greedo to soak up my one destiny, and I decide to lose Luke rather than peel 7. That's a setback that I never recover from, I struggle to get characters in hand, and in a couple turns he has every Tatooine BG on lock down, and I'm getting drained for 5-6 a turn. I throw down a few more guys in a vain effort to get a foothold anywhere I can, but it's quickly apparent that the Force isn't with me and I scoop. Not even sure if Batmouse had anything in his lost pile at this point. On the plus side, that leaves me with about half an hour to grab a snack, and a smoke break, and try to clear my head in hopes of salvaging a 2-2 finish.

    Loss (1-2)

    Game 4 - BONUS ROUND - First Order Deal vs Matt's WYS

    So I'm actually given a bye in this round. But Roy decides he hates Star Wars cards and doesn't want to play. Or he feels sympathetic that I flew the whole way down and was only going to play three games. Either way he offers me his seat at the table in this round, and I graciously accept.

    Matt seems unsure of how to tackle this deck, so I feel comfortable that he's going to stay off Bespin for a couple turns, and I'll have a chance to get set up. Also helps that I open hand TMNALTC for the first time in like 30 games played with this deck. I also open hand Executor, but Matt still shield busts within the first couple turns playing grabber, DDTA, Goldenrod, and Battle Plan. This time I do get set up on turn 3, and Matt can't play Ultimatum so I'm getting in a solid drain/ping of 8 per turn. Also helps that I draw up Strategic Reserves on turn 2, and can start blocking Kessel/Cantina drains right away. He eventually goes to Bespin and the Executor survives a furious onslaught from different combinations of Han/Talon/Falcon, Dash/Outrider, and Mirax/Wedge/Pulsar. Imperial Commands keep the destinies limited, and I keep deploying/reacting TIEs and taking them back into hand. There are some other battles at the East Platform but I win all of them, and without Aim High out, Phasma keeps retrieving troopers. Eventually Chewie is sent to CC on a suicide mission, gets overflowed and it's gg.

    Win (2-2)

    The last game doesn't technically count, so I finish 7th. Still, a 2-2 performance with only one blowout exceeds any expectations I had coming in, and most importantly, I had a lot of fun. The event wraps early, a few of us grab a beer and some grub, and Matt is kind enough to drive me back to the airport....where I get to burn about 3 hours after my flight is delayed.

    Props:

    The whole SoCal crew for being super welcoming to a new face. All great guys, and I'll definitely be down again.

    Ryan J for going 4-0 and taking home the glass.

    You, for reading all of this.

    TSA in Oakland and Burbank for not bothering to go through my bag packed with full deck boxes.

    Slops:

    TSA in Oakland and Burbank for not bothering to go through my bag packed with full deck boxes. Seriously, I've read that those things look like solid black bricks on a scanner, you should really be checking to see what they are.

    Me for some sloppy table etiquette, and too often not announcing phase changes, end of turns, etc. Another area where I guess GEMP has spoiled me. I'm sure that'll get better with more experience.

    Southwest for delaying my return flight and getting home about 2 hours later than expected. Still worth it though!
